programme.title: What the FT Story on China’s Poverty Didn’t Show You
programme.desc: A recent Financial Times article questioning China’s claim of eradicating poverty has sparked widespread debate over accuracy, narrative framing, and the use of evidence.\nIs this a case of healthy skepticism—or selective storytelling?\nHost Ge Anna speaks with Prof. Robert Walker, who was interviewed for the piece and says key parts of his explanation on China’s poverty alleviation efforts were omitted from the report. In his response article, Media Mythmaking: Mistake, Mischief or Malevolence?, he argues the real issue is not criticism itself, but how selective framing shapes perception.

programme.title: Headline：A Chinese village run by a CEO
programme.desc: In a Dai village called \"Manluanzhan\" near China's southwestern border, a full-time rural CEO manages the books and coordinates business operations at homestays, cafés, breweries, and other shops. But how to benefit from rural tourism without losing the village charm?\n\nIn Manluanzhan, a fresh experiment is unfolding – one where villagers remain participants, investors, and decision-makers, but a CEO enters the fray to help defend their interests.

programme.title: Meet China: Flying into the Future, Growing a Greener City, and Connecting Business to the World
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we explore how the future is taking shape across different corners of China and beyond. From Guangzhou's rising low-altitude economy powered by electric flying cars, to Xiamen's practical path toward zero-carbon urban life, we see how innovation is changing the way people live and cities grow. We also step into China's booming livestream shopping culture, where commerce becomes community, and travel to Malaysia's rice fields, where Chinese agricultural expertise is helping improve harvests and food security. This episode reveals how technology, industry and creativity are turning bold ideas into everyday reality.

programme.title: Live: Beyond the buzz: What do young Americans really think about China-US relations?
programme.desc: What happens when young Americans experience China beyond the headlines? Join CGTN for a candid conversation with US creators and students living in China as they share firsthand perspectives on daily life, consumer trends, innovation, and how these experiences are reshaping their understanding of China's economic dynamism and China-US connections.

programme.title: China's Industrial Chains: Threads of Resilience
programme.desc: What is clothing made from? Not just cotton or wool. Sometimes, it starts with a single drop of oil! Follow CGTN as we reveal how a drop of crude oil transforms into our clothes, uncovering a complex and fascinating journey of the textile and garment manufacturing process. \nFollow CGTN's Wang Tianyu and take a closer look at China's textile and garment industry, and unravel the threads that connect China's industrial past, present and future.
